newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed, seen stable for months.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed, seen stable for months.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Wednesday on tiny foreign deals, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.02 points to 174.32 on $8.59 million in volume.

"The market is crawling back and forth like a snail," said Andrei Kukk, chief trader from Rinaco-Plus brokerage. "There are orders exactly enough for several big brokerages to satisfy them easily and make a tiny profit."
He forecast the current state of the market would last for several months.

Oleg Martynenko, head of the sales and trade department at Bank Rossiisky Kredit, said there was demand from Western operators for second-tier shares, which were less speculative as investors needed to assess the companies' health before buying.
Kukk said there was a big order for Surgutneftegaz, which made the price rise by about five to six points in the afternoon, only to sink by about four percent after the order had been fulfilled.
Surgutneftegaz edged up to $0.384 from $0.381 at Tuesday's close, ending off a $0.389 high.
But he said the market was unlikely to retreat strongly as even Gazprom, whose company rules make it difficult to buy its shares, was not falling despite "a sea of offers" from the regions.
"It is a good sign that even Gazprom with all its unfavourable system of re-registration is not falling," Kukk said. "It means that other shares will not fall."
Gazprom rose to $0.320 from $0.315, Norilsk Nickel was $6.70 after $6.75, LUKoil rose to $9.56 from $9.30 and UES fell to $0.0770 from $0.0779.
